row.evidence: ThreatQ's help centre lists Local, 2-Step, LDAP and SAML authentication, where SAML 'User accounts are created and authenticated outside of the ThreatQ platform'; neither the help centre nor the REST API reference v6.16.0 documents a SCIM endpoint.
row.notes: No SCIM by absence (rule 5): threatq.com has no pricing page (/pricing 404; demo request only, quote-only), and the help-centre sitemap (1,070 pages), authentication and user-management docs and REST API reference v6.16.0 have no SCIM. SAML SSO maps IdP attributes to ThreatQ roles; LDAP/AD is the other directory option. Users can also be managed via the REST /users endpoints (administrator permissions). The homepage promotes Securonix (ThreatQuotient's parent); the product is still sold as ThreatQ.

auth.notes: OAuth 2.0 token from POST /token (password grant) using a ThreatQ user account; token times out.

limitations.text: User endpoints need super or administrator permissions.
SAML and LDAP users cannot be edited from the User Management page.

okta.notes: okta.com/integrations/threatq/ and /threatquotient/ return 404. ThreatQ's own Okta pages are threat-intel integrations (Okta CDF/Action), not sign-in apps.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP / Active Directory authentication with role mapping (self-hosted instances)
fallbacks.notes: jit inferred from the docs saying SAML user accounts are created and authenticated outside ThreatQ, with roles mapped from SAML attributes; the docs do not use the term JIT.

citations.title: Authentication Methods
citations.quote: User accounts are created and authenticated outside of the ThreatQ platform and user roles are mapped from the user's Active Directory. Due to this, user accounts cannot be modified within the ThreatQ platform (User Management page).
